#3310. WhatsApp may soon replace the Communities tab on iOS

Some WhatsApp beta testers on iOS are seeing a new option in the app’s bottom navigation bar that replaces the Communities tab. Here are the details.

Over the past few years, WhatsApp has increasingly focused on Communities as more people have turned to messaging platforms to interact in smaller, more private groups rather than through traditional social networks.

At the same time, WhatsApp has been testing several features that make it easier for users to see which of their contacts are online and available to chat.

Back in May, WABetaInfo found that WhatsApp was developing a new Contacts hub that would bring together users’ favorite contacts, as well as those who were currently online or had recently been active.

A few weeks later, WhatsApp began testing a new green dot indicator on iOS to make it easier to identify contacts who were online.

Now, WABetaInfo reports that WhatsApp is rolling out the new Contacts hub to some iOS beta testers, replacing the Communities tab in the app’s bottom navigation bar.

The new tab includes a section with favorite contacts and a full contact list. Users can see their favorite contacts at the top of the screen, making it easier to start a conversation with them. They can also sort the full contact list by activity, alphabetical, and birthdays. With alphabetical, the app organizes contacts by name. With activity, WhatsApp shows who is currently online at the top of the list. WhatsApp marks these contacts with a green dot, so users can easily distinguish them from offline contacts. WhatsApp also sorts recently active contacts by last seen, so users can quickly identify who was active most recently. With birthdays, WhatsApp sorts contacts by their upcoming birthday, so users can see who has a birthday coming up soon.

The site notes that the new tab also allows users to add contacts directly, with the option to sync them to their iPhone’s address book.

As for Communities, the feature itself isn’t going away, but rather being moved to a dedicated filter in the Chats tab.

WABetaInfo also notes that WhatsApp is experimenting with potentially replacing the Updates tab, rather than Communities, with the Contacts tab in a future configuration.

For now, the new Contacts tab is available to a limited number of beta testers running the latest WhatsApp beta for iOS via TestFlight, with a broader rollout expected over the coming weeks.

To read WABetaInfo’s full report, follow this link.

#3308. This Actively Exploited Chrome Vulnerability Is Putting Your Browser at Risk

If you've seen an uptick in security updates as of late, you're not alone. AI models have become very good at finding new security vulnerabilities throughout 2026. Researchers and hackers alike are increasingly relying on these models in their individual pursuits: Hackers want to find these flaws to exploit them, while researchers want to block hackers from doing so. Microsoft's latest Patch Tuesday update included more than 1,400 patches; meanwhile, Apple's latest security update fixed two iMessage flaws that let both bad actors and innocent parties alike access texts they shouldn't.

Whether you use a Mac or a PC, you probably browse the web with Chrome, or a Chromium-based browser. As it happens, Google's web browsing platform is the latest to receive an important security update—but it's far from the first important Chrome update of the year.

As reported by The Hacker News, Google released a new update for Chrome on Monday that patches nine security flaws. While all vulnerabilities are important to patch, one in particular is more serious than the rest: CVE-2026-125350, a use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component.

Use-after-free vulnerabilities happen when the system frees up a memory location, but a program tries to access it anyway. It's a glitch in programming, but it offers bad actors an opportunity to break into your system. At worst, it allows arbitrary code execution, or, in other words, gives hackers the ability to run their own code in the app or system.

That's bad enough on the surface, but, unfortunately, Google confirmed that CVE-2026-125350 has an active exploit in the wild. The company is keeping other details close to the vest, but it's dangerous nonetheless. At least someone, somewhere, has used this flaw against a target, which puts all Chrome users (as well as users of Chromium-based browsers) at risk.

What's more, this isn't Chrome's first active exploit of the year—this is its eighth. The company is playing catch-up with hackers looking to target users of its browser, which makes sense, seeing as Chrome is by far the world's most popular browser.

If you're using Chrome on your computer, you'll want to update it as soon as possible. Make sure you're running at least versions 157.0.8103.50/.51 on Mac or PC, or 157.0.8103.50 on Linux. To check, click the three dots in the top-right corner of your Chrome window, then go to More > Help > About Google Chrome.

Other Chromium-based browsers may not have the update yet, but they are affected by this flaw. If you use browsers like Microsoft Edge, Opera, or Brave, keep an eye on your updates to install any of the latest patches.

#3307. HomeKit Weekly: SwitchBot’s Curtain Track 4 is the easiest smart curtain retrofit yet

The worst part of owning smart curtain motors is charging them, because it usually means taking the whole motor down from the track or running a really long USB cord to charge it. Today, SwitchBot has released the SwitchBot Curtain Track 4 aimed at solving that problem with a battery module that detaches on its own, so the motor stays in place, and you only take down the part that needs to charge.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

The SwitchBot Curtain Track 4 is a retrofit motor for curtains that hang on a U-rail track. You hang it on the track between the curtain hooks, run a one-tap calibration in the SwitchBot app, and your existing curtains can then be motorized and used in your smart home. There’s no drilling, no rewiring, and no need to position magnets to stick to the rail, as earlier SwitchBot curtain motors required. SwitchBot claims the whole setup takes about 30 seconds.

One thing to check first: this version is for U-rail tracks only, not curtain rods.

The Battery+ version pairs a small built-in battery with a detachable 5,000mAh module for a total of 6,400mAh. SwitchBot rates it at up to 12 months of use for each charge, depending on curtain weight and movement frequency. When it needs charging, you pull the module off, charge it via USB-C, and clip it back on. SwitchBot also sells a Solar version that uses a small panel to keep the battery topped off if the window gets enough sun.

The motor itself connects via Bluetooth, so getting it into Apple Home requires a compatible SwitchBot Hub, which brings it there via Matter. Once it’s there, the curtains work like any other window covering in your Home app. You can add them to scenes, control them with Siri, and include multiple windows in a single automation. It’s always nice to time smart curtains/shades with dusk/dawn as well.

SwitchBot’s built-in QuietDrift mode opens the curtains slowly in the morning, at about half a centimeter per second, so the room fills with daylight gradually rather than all at once. SwitchBot says it runs at around 25 dB in that mode. You can also give the curtain a gentle tug by hand and the motor takes over, which is great if you don’t have your iPhone with you or someone doesn’t have access to your Apple Home setup.

SwitchBot built it in a way to correct drift over time, so you shouldn’t need to recalibrate it if it gets off.

The SwitchBot Curtain Track 4 turns the U-rail curtains you already have into Apple Home window coverings without replacing anything. The detachable battery is the best feature here, as it lets you charge it without a long cord.

The SwitchBot Curtain Track 4 is available now on Amazon and directly from SwitchBot.

#3306. The 15 Best ‘Hunger Games’ Soundtrack Songs

In the opening scene of The Hunger Games, before the battle and bloodshed, Katniss Everdeen comforts her sister Prim with a lullaby. “Deep in the meadow, under the willow,” she sings. “A bed of grass, a soft green pillow.” It only lasts a few seconds, enough to get out two simple lyrics, but it tells us what’s most important to Katniss, played by Jennifer Lawrence, and how she communicates. It tells us just how essential music is to the narrative about to unfold.

The Hunger Games franchise has grown considerably since the release of the first film in 2012. The four-part saga, adapted from the book trilogy written by Suzanne Collins, concluded in 2015. Since then, the franchise has expanded with two more book-to-film prequel pairings. The most musical of the batch, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, received a theatrical release in 2023, while the latest installment, Sunrise on the Reaping, was released in theaters on Friday, Nov. 20.

Each film has arrived alongside eclectic, star-studded soundtracks that recruit artists with distinct interpretations of the highly emotional, hotly volatile story at the heart of The Hunger Games. They aren’t all soothing lullabies, mockingjay calls, or political anthems. But they are genre-spanning, and rich with characters we’ve seen go from the page to the screen. With original releases created by artists from Lorde, Patti Smith, and the Weekend to Olivia Rodrigo, Taylor Swift, and Bella Kay, here are the 15 best Hunger Games soundtrack songs.

“Yellow Flicker Beat,” the first song released from the Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 1 soundtrack, opens with an unsettling hum. In 2014, Lorde described the song as her first attempt at getting inside of Katniss’ head. From the beginning, the character served as a flicker of hope for the districts, but the worst nightmare who leaders in the Capitol never saw coming. All over the song, you can hear the threads of teenage angst and rebellion that colored Lorde’s debut album Pure Heroine. It’s present in the opening verse, when she compares her blood to rubies and precious stones, but especially when the chorus hits: “This is the start of how it all ends/They used to shout my name, now they whisper it.” — Larisha Paul

Before Folklore and Evermore, Taylor Swift wrote from the perspective of one bow-slinging fictional character in particular: Katniss Everdeen. The result was “Safe & Sound,” a folky lullaby carried by plucky chords that pierce to the bone as they push against the salve-like lyrics. Swift and T-Bone Burnett, the architect behind the first Hunger Games soundtrack, captured the eerie energy of that initial film during an impromptu writing and recording session in Los Angeles with the help of the Civil Wars, who offer haunting harmonies. “The Civil Wars had a show that night so they raced right over to T Bone’s house,” Swift told Rolling Stone in 2012. “There’s so many things he could’ve done production-wise to make that song bigger sonically than it is, but I think that would have possibly been a mistake. For [Burnett] to have left the song as a lullaby is brilliant.” —M.G.

Olivia Rodrigo channels her songbird best on this acoustic taunt, sung from the perspective of The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds Snakes character, Lucy Gray Baird, “[She] is a character that I feel very connected to,” Rodrigo said in 2022. She packs the song with a convincing sense of vengeance atop the kind of gorgeous melody that a mockingjay would love to repeat. In fact, the closing credits song was inspired by the film’s final aerial scene of the fictional birds. “That was playing in a loop in my head over and over, and I was like, ‘I want to write a song that captures what that feeling is.’ That was the goal,” she said. —Maya Georgi

Tinashe didn’t originally write “The Leap” with the chaotic rebellion of The Hunger Games in mind. It was meant for one of her own albums, but at the time, Lorde — 17 at the time — was tasked with curating the Mockingjay – Part 1 soundtrack, and her team wanted to see what Tinashe might contribute. “The Leap” provides a sharp and chilling parallel to the film. “I’m gonna set it all ablaze, watch it burn to ash and dust,” calls to the destruction of Katniss’ home, District 12. “I was waiting on you, waiting on you” calls to Petta being stuck in the Capitol. And “hurry up, don’t miss your chance” nods to the harrowing secrets that come to light throughout the film. Even by accident, Tinashe hit her mark with “The Leap.” —L.P.

The first time we hear “The Hanging Tree” in the Hunger Games, it’s in the soft tone of Jennifer Lawrence’s voice. In Mockingjay, the rebellion begins to take full shape with Katniss at its heart. It’s a protest song for the ages. “Are you, are you/Coming to the tree/Where they strung up a man they say murdered three,” she sang. “Strange things did happen here/No stranger would it be/If we met up at midnight in the hanging tree.” In The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, when Rachel Zegler’s Lucy Gray Baird sings its sweet melody, we learn it was written following an execution in District 12. The prequel film takes place more than six decades before the events of the first film in the original trilogy. “The Hanging Tree,” like the mockingjay’s call, is the musical thread that ties them together. —L.P.

In Catching Fire, Katniss Everdeen and 23 other former Hunger Games victors head back into the arena. It’s an act of vengeance from President Snow, to show that even in victory, their lives still do not belong to themselves. The sob that breaks through when the format of the 75th Hunger Games is revealed in the film is unforgettable and devastating. On the sparse soundtrack cut “Devil May Cry,” the Weeknd offers a silver lining. “It won’t be in vain/To swallow all your pain,” he sings. “And learn to love what burns/And gather courage to return.” It’s all the tributes-turned victors-turned tributes again have to hold onto. —L.P.

The National originally titled their contribution to the Catching Fire soundtrack “Dying Is Easy.” On one hand, there’s some truth to the title, especially in the context of the Hunger Games. A momentary distraction in the arena, a step off of the starting line just a second early, any hesitation — it could all end in a flash. On the other hand, the final title, “Lean,” feels more apt to the theme of reliance that emerges throughout the song. “Dying is easy/I believe my love and my love relieves me,” Matt Berninger sings, later accepting the consequences of holding care in your heart in a battle as callous as the one in this story: “Love will lead us all to smithereens.” —L.P.

This is … the mocking as the jay, or rather, Patti Smith’s unique interpretation of Katniss as her character helps set the rebellion aflame in the Catching Fire film. The punk rock poet offers her best spoken-word couplets on this smoldering, folky take that’s less in the vein of “People Have the Power” and more of “Easter.” Leave it to Smith to tap into her political heart to speak truth to power, even when it’s about a fictionalized tyranny. —M.G.

Gigi Perez is somehow able to balance yearning, loss, and tenderness through the husky, low pitch of her voice, and she brought all those feelings to “Favor,” a haunting, folk-driven cut from The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping soundtrack. The acoustic track is emotional as it captures the goodbye between Haymitch and Lenore. Perez gets to the core of longing and missing someone, singing, “When you arе lonely, know I’m awake, listen for me and the song that we sang.” —Julyssa Lopez

Bella Kay continues the tradition of young, breakthrough singer-songwriters lending their musical and emotional expertise to The Hunger Games. “See It Coming,” from the Sunrise on the Reaping soundtrack, is a refusal to be blindsided: “Tell me you run, I’m beggin’ you, hide/They’re gonna hurt you, so give ’em a fight,” Kay sings, the distinct country twang that only occasionally slips through present in her tone. “A little revenge, an eye for an eye/We can call it a draw.” It cuts to the heart of the Hunger Games musical universe: to still feel and love deeply even in the face of impossible survival. The opening verse takes us back to the beginning while looking towards an uncertain future. “Swear to me now you’ll remember me hummin’,” she sings. —L.P.

Appearing on the Mockingjay Part 1 soundtrack, this Charli XCX contribution feels like an ember of hope hidden underneath the rubble of the Second Rebellion of Panem. Led by a cascading piano melody, Charli assumes the role of Katniss near the end of the original Hunger Games series; she’s bruised, beaten, and grief-stricken, but must go on. For a brief moment, Duran Duran’s Simon Le Bon appears to support her on the Rostam and Ariel Rechtshaid-produced rallying cry. “I’m lost, but I can’t slow,” Charli coos, before leaving the listener with an inspiring message: “I’m lost, but not alone.” —Jaeden Pinder

Ushered in like a gospel prayer, Miranda Lambert recruited her Pistol Annies bandmates Ashley Monroe and Angaleena Presley for “Run Daddy Run,” which appeared on the first Hunger Games soundtrack. It soon moves into a menacing warning: “Daddy, can you hear the devil drawing near” the trio sings in a gorgeous but unsettling harmony. “Like a bullet from a gun, run daddy run.” It’s a haunting warning that captures the alarm of the first film. —Marissa Moss

The Chemical Brothers and Miguel may seem an unlikely union, but the rebellious spirit of their Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 1 collaboration “This Is Not a Game” works despite the odds. The skittering electronic track opens with a whisper from Lorde, who extended her curatorial duties to include vocal contributions, singing, “There it is.” Miguel comes out swinging in the first verse with a quote from Charles Bukowski: “Find what you love and let it kill you.” He spends the rest of the song pouring gasoline on the fire of revolution, while the Chemical Brothers turn up the dial on their dark, warping production and pull trap influences into the fold. “I know what I’m doing,” Miguel spits. —L.P.

Before Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark were even born, there was Lucy Gray Baird. This District 12 tribute with a rebel heart knew that she had to charm the fake eyelashes off the Capitol if she wanted any chance at a victory, and so she did with this song. In The Ballad of the Songbirds and Snakes book, Gray Baird tells the devastating tale of her fated life with a guitar and Appalachian-inspired drawl during her pre-Games interview. With lyrics like “It’s sooner than later that I’m six feet under /It’s sooner than later that you’ll be alone,” it’s a sobering listen. Thankfully, Rachel Zegler does the pivotal moment justice with this soulful rendition, each bruised line made more powerful by her quivering soprano. —M.G.

Mckenna Grace joins the Hunger Games franchise in two roles, as both Maysilee Donner and Merrilee Donner in Sunrise on the Reaping. She holds the emotional anguish of both characters close on “Half Alive,” a sprawling soundtrack cut that confronts death and the destruction it brings, especially when it’s for the sake of entertainment. “I say I’m mean and tough and I don’t care ‘cause I’m not weak,” she sings. “But if tomorrow was my last, hope someone mourns me/Watch as they all applaud.” There are times during the song where Grace sounds breathless, grasping at a calmness that will always evade her. During the chorus, she pleads for whatever version of it she can get: “We feel the unspoken, the look in your eyes/Promise you’ll hold me when I’m half alive.” —L.P.

When it comes to cleaning tasks, I’ve always relied on my trusted white vinegar to come to the rescue. Be it cleaning surface stains or giving my windows a streak-free finish, there are so many uses for white vinegar around the home.

But why exactly are people spraying vinegar on their front doors this season? While your first thought might be to simply clean the surface thoroughly, you’ll be mistaken.

According to a University of Minnesota Extension study, diluted white vinegar can deter pests like ants and spiders from taking refuge in your home. So all of a sudden, layering it on your front door makes sense. Here’s why.

It seems like white vinegar can do so much more than cleaning and limescale removal; it also makes a great natural ant and pest repellent. Not only do ants have a highly sensitive sense of smell and can be overwhelmed by the strong vinegar odor, but it can also clean up ant pheromone paths — disrupting them from guiding others toward food and moisture sources.

Essentially, spraying white vinegar eliminates the chemical scent trails ants leave behind, helping to prevent an infestation in your home. Which is why it’s a good idea to target potential entryways such as around the front door frame, baseboards, and cracks.

Essentially, spraying white vinegar eliminates the chemical scent trails ants leave behind, helping to prevent an infestation in your home.

Bear in mind that using vinegar is only a short-term fix rather than a long-term deterrent.

And this isn’t guaranteed to banish a persistent pest problem or a full infestation. In that case, it’s always best to call a professional local pest control service to handle it.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Simply mix equal parts white vinegar and water in a spray bottle to create a mild solution. Then, spray this mixture around your front door, making sure to target any small gaps or crevices where ants might enter. This process helps erase chemical trails left by ants and temporarily interrupts their activity. What’s more, it’s cheap, chemical-free, and only takes seconds to do.

Also, since white vinegar has a high acidity level, take care to protect nearby plants and sensitive surfaces from potential damage.

Alternatively, experts advise soaking cotton wool balls in peppermint essential oil before putting them around door frames. The strong fragrance will be too overpowering for such pests and will prevent them from entering.

This pure peppermint oil is paraben free, and provides a fresh scent. Versatile to use in aromatherapy, or in an oil or reed diffuser. And while the fragrance is pleasant to our senses, it is also known to be a natural pest repellent.

For more pest tips, be sure to clear this one thing in their yard to prevent rats this fall.

NOTE: Do NOT use peppermint oil if you have pets as this is toxic when inhaled or ingested.

#3303. High-Protein Packaged Foods May Not Be As Healthy As They Look

Of the three major macronutrients—protein, carbs, and fat—protein has the best reputation, and it’s fairly well deserved. We need significant amounts of protein in our diet, and nothing particularly bad happens if we get too much. Dietary protein helps you build muscle, and if you’re trying to lose weight it helps stop you from losing too much muscle along with the fat. It also helps to make meals feel filling. Great! But.

Once the general public gets the idea that something is good for you, the companies that make packaged food start putting it in everything. Or, they make products where the good-for-you thing features prominently on the label, whether or not there is very much inside. So a lot of packaged food now boasts protein on the label. Here’s what you should ask yourself about those foods:

Take a close look here—sometimes a food will boast of a certain amount of protein per package but the package contains two or three servings. Other times, the protein per serving is correct, and we're supposed to be excited to have, say, 7 grams per serving. That's just not very much—and certainly not worth paying extra or choosing a less-delicious food just for those few added grams.

It’s good to know how much protein you need in your diet. If you’re not gaining or losing weight, and not doing very much exercise, a 150-pound person only needs about 54 grams of protein a day. (I've done the math for various body weights here.) If you’re working out a lot, or if you’re trying to gain or lose weight (yep, either way), that same 150-pound person will need more like 81 to 95 grams of protein per day. More is OK, but not necessary.

So if you’re trying to get 90 grams per day, 30 grams per meal is a reasonable amount to shoot for. Coincidentally, 30 grams is the amount of protein that tends to make a meal feel satisfying. You can do the math to figure out whether a protein-added product is going to be helpful in your day’s diet.

I think this is the most important question about protein-added foods. It’s not hard to get protein in a meal; meats, dairy, tofu, beans, and grains all tend to supply plenty. So what is this protein-added thing you’re considering, and are you eating it instead of a traditional meal?

Here’s an example. If I’m heading straight from the gym to run some errands, and I need something to substitute for a meal—yeah, this isn’t great planning, but sometimes it happens—a protein bar with 20 grams of protein is a step in the right direction. Much better than a candy bar, anyway.

But then there are things like this "protein mix" trail mix: 7 grams of protein with 200 calories. A double serving would be 400 calories and only 14 grams of protein. Hardly a great choice if your goal is just to add to your protein intake for the day.

And then there are the chips that my kid, for a time, couldn't stop eating. He loves Doritos and such; on a whim, we bought him some protein chips (yes, these are a real thing). Are they better for him than the equivalent amount of Doritos? Arguably, sort of yes. But then he started arguing that since they have protein, he should be able to eat them in place of dinner. We nixed that, but admit it: Are you having that same argument with yourself, feeling better about a snack food because it contains extra protein? If so, the marketing is working—you’re feeling good about your supposedly healthy choices, even though you’re just eating a bag of chips.

#3302. If you bought an iPhone Duo, have you kept or returned it? [Poll]

When Apple announced the iPhone Duo back in September, the company called it “the most transformational change to iPhone since the original,” and there’s no doubt that it generated a huge amount of excitement.

But a new report suggests that for some buyers the novelty quickly wore off, and they ended up returning their devices. Is this just a handful of people, or is it more common … ?

It’s been a very long time since any smartphone launch has generated quite so much buzz. Apple called it a breakthrough in iPhone design.

iPhone Duo features a breakthrough foldable design that’s beautiful, versatile, and durable, opening up possibilities that feel entirely new yet remarkably familiar […]

“iPhone Duo is the most transformational change to iPhone since the original. With an entirely new design and intuitive experiences, it shows what’s possible when hardware and software are engineered together and redefines what it means to use a foldable phone,” said John Ternus.

Despite not really being the target market for the phone, I was still wowed by the launch video and remained incredibly impressed when I got some hands-on time with one.

Many couldn’t resist buying one despite the price – but The Verge notes that not everyone has ending up keeping the device. Apple allows you to return any product within 14 days for a full refund without having to give any reason. That window has come to an end for some of the first buyers and the site’s Alison Johnson spoke with some of those who’d decided to take advantage of it.

The iPhone Duo replaced both my iPhone 15 Pro Max and my iPad Mini 6. It now is my phone and iPad mini in my pocket. This is the dream phone I never knew I wanted.

And for the lack of Face ID, Touch ID works perfect with my Apple Watch. And even without wearing it, I don’t see the big deal of the ‘huge’ effort of bringing my finger to a button.

For the lacking 5x zoom that I had on my Pro Max, I haven’t had a moment yet that I wanted to use it to be honest. Those moments will definitely arise, but the lack of that camera cannot go up against the amazing overall experience of the iPhone Duo.

But the more fundamental reason for some is that it hasn’t really lived up to their hopes for a multifunctional device.

“If I can have an iPad in my pocket, that would be great.” So thought Ben Seligson, a content creator, photographer, and now former iPhone Duo owner […] “Usually I’d throw a YouTube video on the iPad or throw a podcast up. And then I start cooking dinner and leave my iPad in one spot, but I’d have my phone in my pocket if I got a text, or I needed to set a timer or something like that.” With the Duo, the phone was also the iPad on the counter, so a quick reply became much more of an interruption.

I’m curious as to whether this is just a small minority of buyers or a more common phenomenon. If you bought a Duo early enough to have hit the end of the return window, please take our poll to let us know whether you decided to keep it or return it – and do share your reasons in the comments (which are now back).

Oh, and the good news for anyone buying one now is that you’ll have a lot longer to make up your mind, with the extended return window for the holidays in place. You can now return anything bought today through January 8.

#3300. How the Biopic ‘Being Heumann’ Pulls Off Two Revolutions

Judy Heumann is just trying to cross the road in her wheelchair. It’s New York City in the 1970s, and the streets are chaotic. Traffic barrels past, pedestrians crowd the sidewalks, and the concrete curbs are steep cliffs. Unable to get her wheelchair up onto the sidewalk, she rolls in the middle of Madison Avenue, giving the middle finger to a city bus driver behind her who is laying on his horn.

Set to the propulsive guitar riff of Iggy Pop’s proto-punk anthem “The Passenger,” the opening sequence of Being Heumann — a new biopic about the disability-advocacy pioneer — introduces a woman who refuses to be dismissed and has zero patience for anyone standing in her way as she navigates through potholes, puddles, and pedestrians.

“You are not introduced quietly to this character,” says Ruth Madeley, who portrays Heumann. “You literally meet her in utter chaos and noise. She’s unfazed because she is doing that every damn day of her life.”

Denied access to school until she was nine years old because administrators considered her and her wheelchair a fire hazard, Heumann later sued the New York Board of Education for the right to become a teacher. Her fight for equal access grew into a lifelong crusade.

In 1970, she co-founded Disabled in Action, a grassroots advocacy organization, and went on to become a leading voice in the independent living movement. Her activism helped pave the way for landmark legislation including the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Audacious, confident, and fiercely determined, Heumann became known as the “mother of the disability rights movement,” helping to transform disability from a matter of charity into a question of civil rights.

Siân Heder, the 2022 Oscar-winning director of CODA, first encountered Judy Heumann in the 2020 Sundance-winning documentary Crip Camp. When she read Heumann’s memoir, from which the film takes its title, Heder saw a fascinating contradiction in a leader who demanded humanity from the world but sometimes struggled to recognize the limitations of those around her. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

In Being Heumann (now streaming on Apple TV), we see Judy charismatically inspire fellow disabled activists into action. And we also see when she pushes them to take on more risk than their bodies might be able to endure, like a hunger strike she urged others to take part in, even if that wasn’t wise considering their medical conditions.

“The title took on these other levels of meaning,” Heder says, “where it’s as much about Judy having to learn how to be human as it is about her asking the world to treat this marginalized group of people as human.”

For Madeley, portraying the fierce and complicated civil rights icon was “the biggest acting undertaking of my life. Finally, I get to play somebody who gets things wrong? Who is kind of brash sometimes? Who is so focused that she sometimes can alienate people,” Madeley says.

After the opening scene in New York City, we fast forward five years to April 1977 San Francisco. Rather than attempt to chronicle Heumann’s entire extraordinary life, Heder and her co-writer Rebekah Taussig focused the film on Heumann’s organization of a sit-in protest for Section 504, the first federal law that protects against discrimination based on disability. Heumann and her coalition of more than 100 disabled protesters staged the longest peaceful occupation of a federal building in U.S. history.

But Being Heumann isn’t your typical reverent biopic or a pedantic history lesson. Heder turns the fight for Section 504 and disability-rights legislation into a kind of high-stakes caper – an outrageous pursuit of an almost impossible prize.  Related Content Disabled Fans Say the Live-Music Industry Can Do Better: ‘We Are Not a Pain in the Ass’ The DOJ Is Stocking Its Civil Rights Division With Right-Wing Kooks ‘Un-American’: Dems Dig in as Southern States Try to Eliminate Black Representation Justice Department Guts Voting Rights Unit: Report

Heder recalls, “When I got to the section on the 504 [protest], I thought, ‘Oh, this is Dog Day Afternoon with disabled people. This is a bank robbery with people who don’t know how to rob a bank.'”

”This is a heist movie with a group of people who no one would expect to see in a heist movie,” Madeley says. “They weren’t going in for money or jewels. They were going for their rights. It was so much more expensive and so much more precious.”

EVERY GREAT HEIST HAS a plan within the plan, a twist the audience never saw coming. For Being Heumann, that second heist happened behind the camera. “Judy’s next mountain, her next mission, was Hollywood,” Madeley says.

Before her death in 2023, Heumann turned her attention toward the entertainment industry’s dismal record on disability representation. A 2019 Ford Foundation study authored by Heumann revealed “that disabled people were one in four in the population, and the media representation was under three percent,” according to Heder. “When disabled roles came up, they were played by non-disabled people.”

Some of this discrimination may be due, Heder says, to archaic ideas about the physical grit required for the job. “There’s an ethos around filmmaking where you die for the movie, and it’s like war, and it’s a badge of honor that you can’t walk at the end of every day. And what it’s done is exclude a lot of really talented people who can’t be on their feet for 14 hours,” Heder says.

Committed to upending that status quo, Heder hired widely from the disabled community. Being Heumann features 12 disabled leads and, at times, up to 60 disabled background performers. She was also determined to address inaccessibility on set. While the art department filled in modern curb cuts to recreate the inaccessible streets of the 1970s, the Being Heumann accessibility team was simultaneously building ramps, installing lifts and modifying trailers to make the set accessible.

For Madeley, who uses a wheelchair, the difference was transformative. “To have accessibility completely cared for, I was able to show up every day as an actor, and I didn’t realize how liberating that was.”

The film’s most powerful intersection of historical activism and present-day disability experience comes during a congressional testimony sequence. One by one, the disabled protesters share the indignities and injustices that have shaped their lives. Heder invited the actors to draw from their own experiences, blurring the boundaries between historical reenactment and personal testimony.

“I met with each actor and asked them what aspect of their experience they would be interested to share. What followed was one of the most powerfully cathartic experiences I’ve ever had on a set,” Heder says. “We rolled the camera in one long take, allowing actors to take turns coming up to the microphone. I sat by the camera and interviewed them, sometimes as their characters and sometimes as themselves.”

The scene transforms a decades-old debate about federal regulations into a profoundly contemporary portrait of discrimination, dignity, and belonging. “We were building something bigger than us. Whatever the outcome of the movie, we were allowing people who had been unseen and unheard to be centered,” Heder says.

AFTER 26 DAYS, THE protesters in San Francisco achieved what many believed impossible. Secretary of Health, Education and Welfare Joseph Califano (played in the film by Mark Ruffalo) signed the Section 504 regulations, establishing enforceable federal protections against disability discrimination and helping lay the groundwork for the Americans With Disabilities Act, passed 13 years later in 1990.

On the final day of filming, Madeley recalls when first assistant director Walter Gasparovic wrapped production by calling out the names of every cast member, including the background performers. Like the activists they portrayed, the cast and crew pulled off something Hollywood long considered impossible — an accessible production with one of the largest ensembles of actors with disabilities in history.

Madeley remembers thinking, “We did it. We pulled off the heist!”

But even in that triumphant moment, she could hear Judy urging them onward. “I could literally feel Judy being like, ‘That’s great! Now get in the edit.’” Because for Judy Heumann, a hard-won victory was never the end of the fight. It was simply the beginning of dismantling the next obstacle.

At the Los Angeles premiere of Being Heumann at AFI Fest, Heder discovered that the historic theater hosting the celebration had an inaccessible stage and backstage area, preventing members of her cast from participating onstage and forcing the Q&A to be relocated to the middle of the auditorium.

Even as Hollywood celebrated a film about disability rights, the building itself was excluding the very people whose story it was honoring. Heder publicly called out the theater during the premiere. “I had to say something because Judy would.” Trending Stories Noel Fielding Says He Regrets 'Horrible' Jokes He Made With Russell Brand After Old Clip Resurfaces Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters Files for Divorce From Fourth Wife Kamilah Chavis After 5 Years of Marriage Can Chris Van Hollen Really Unseat Chuck Schumer? Journey Go Their Separate Ways With Longtime Drummer

“Hollywood’s all about world-building,” Madeley says. “We build buildings. We build car chases. We build things that we can set on fire. Things are done in the industry that are hard and expensive. Building a ramp is not that big a deal. Hollywood, no more excuses. We’ve done it.”

“Being Heumann” is now streaming on Apple TV, debuting alongside a new accessibility feature offering optional onscreen ASL and BSL interpretation. The film’s sign language interpretation was directed by “CODA” and “Being Heumann” cast member Daniel Durant.

#3295. Why Websites Show the Wrong Server Location When You Use a VPN

There are many reasons why someone might use a VPN, but most often, it’s to conceal your real geographic location or prevent websites from tracking your online activity. It can also be a way to get around location-based restrictions that stop you from accessing certain websites or platforms.

When you connect to a VPN server in the United States, websites are supposed to detect that your online traffic is originating from the U.S. That way, you can access online platforms that use IP filters to block non-U.S. traffic or circumvent regional censorship when travelling outside the U.S. But if you connect to a VPN server in the United States while you’re vacationing in Mexico, and a website thinks your IP address is from Brazil, that might not solve your problem and may even add unnecessary complications.

If you’ve encountered something similar with your VPN provider, there are several fixes you can try. Depending on why your IP location is being misinterpreted, one of these should help you access the internet from the server location of your choice.

IP geolocation isn’t infallible. Websites rely on third-party IP databases to look up your location based on your current IP address. Maxmind, which has one of the largest such databases in existence, claims that its GeoIP products have a 99.8% accuracy. Lesser-known providers with smaller IP databases may be far less accurate.

Websites can also use more than just your IP address to estimate your location. For example, they can send WebRTC requests to your browser or directly query your device’s GPS. Moreover, VPN providers often have physical servers in one country while their IP addresses are registered to another country, and this discrepancy can also create issues. Let’s take a closer look at each of these problems individually, so you can find the fix that works best for you.

WebRTC is an open-source technology that lets your browser reduce latency when engaged in high-bandwidth tasks like streaming or video calls. Based on the IETF standard RFC 8828, it lets a website choose between your VPN server and your real IP address so it can establish the quickest path to transmit large amounts of data and reduce wait times or buffering.

But the catch with WebRTC is that it exposes both your VPN server and ISP-assigned addresses to websites, which can reveal your real IP location and cause websites to reject your VPN server country. Firefox now comes with built-in protections to prevent WebRTC leaks, while Chrome and Edge support third-party extensions like WebRTC Control that you can use to eliminate these issues. To check if your browser is leaking your real IP address during WebRTC requests, you can use a free tool like BrowserLeaks.

Even when a browser isn’t leaking your real IP address, DNS resolvers may fetch inaccurate location information if their nearest servers are too far from your current location. For example, a user in São Paulo may be geolocated to Chile when using Google Public DNS because that’s where Google’s nearest resolvers are located.

If you toggle on DNS leak protection in your VPN app, this will force websites to use your VPN’s resolver to perform DNS lookups. That often solves the problem, but, again, you can confirm the fix worked through a service like BrowserLeaks or IPLeaks.

Websites rely on IP databases like Maxmind, IP2Location, IPinfo, etc. to look up your exact location, but these databases get outdated quickly and need constant updating. Most of these databases also correct errors on request, but that takes some time. Also, each website has its own rules for how often it queries IP databases for updates.

Even when locations are updated in the actual database, a website may be sitting with outdated information unless it actively has refreshed it recently. MaxMind recommends doing this at least twice a week, but that’s ultimately up to the specific website.

VPN providers often rely on virtual servers that use IP addresses registered in a different region than the server’s physical location. For example, ExpressVPN notes that it serves IP addresses in Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela through servers located physically in Brazil.

While this is usually to help with the lack of local infrastructure or strict surveillance laws in the region, many databases and analytics tools will flag the discrepancy for websites, leading to confusion and inconsistency regarding your actual server location. In these cases, your best bet is to switch your VPN server or use a dedicated IP address by signing up for a paid add-on for your VPN.

Before investing in a specific solution, it’s better to do a thorough lookup to make sure why your IP address is pointing to the wrong location and whether a WebRTC or DNS issue, virtual servers, or something else is the cause. Here’s how I’d go about it, step by step:

We’ll start by recording your baseline IP address, country, city, and ASN. With your VPN disconnected, navigate to IPConfig.co on your browser to grab your default IP details. I like this tool because it’s free and uses echoip to pull your location data straight from Maxmind. If you prefer using Terminal instead of your browser, you can also run curl ifconfig.co/json to grab these details in plain text format.

Now connect your VPN server. Then visit IPConfig.co again to note down the changed details.

Make sure the Country and Timezone fields match your current VPN server location. Also make sure the ASN (organization) field does not list your home ISP.

In case these details do not match your VPN server, run a WebRTC leak test and a DNS leak test using BrowserLeaks. If either of these tests doesn’t return your VPN server’s IP address, you’ve found your culprit.

If both the leak tests come back clean but a specific site still gets your location wrong, the issue is likely originating from an outdated database or virtual server.

There’s no surefire way to solve IP location mismatches for good. But if it happens often enough to disrupt your internet use, you can consider switching to a different VPN server and getting a browser add-on that prevents WebRTC leaks. If that doesn’t work, I’d consider buying a dedicated IP address that isn’t based on a virtual server. While many IP databases like MaxMind or IP2Location also have ways to request a location correction, that takes a while to go through and isn’t worth the effort unless it’s a permanent IP address registered through your ISP.

#3292. Could ‘Rubber Soul’ Be the Best Beatles Album? (Yes)

Fall is always Rubber Soul Season. The Beatles’ 1965 masterpiece has always been autumn-coded, with its bristling guitars, wistful vocals, pensive lyrics. But this fall, Rubber Soul has been in the air even more than usual, because of the phenomenal new Special Edition, which gets you up close with John, Paul, George, and Ringo like never before. Their most emotional album. Their moodiest. Their wittiest. Their best.

So what is it that makes Rubber Soul the Beatles’ best album? It’s a loaded question, but for some of us, there’s a correct answer, and it’s simple: It all comes down to the singing. In addition to everything else it is, Rubber Soul is the best place to hear John, Paul, George, and Ringo sing together. It’s four boys telling their stories out loud—you can hear them puzzling out the tales as they sing, bouncing ideas off each other, daring each other to dig a little deeper.

Over the decades, each era chooses its own Beatles album to deify as the ultimate Fabs masterpiece. In the vinyl era, it was Sgt. Pepper; the CD era chose Revolver; the streaming era has anointed Abbey Road. It would be diplomatic and civilized to say that all these albums are equally great…but this will never do, because we all take our own personal Beatles so seriously, and you’d have to be some kind of Mr. Mustard to pretend you don’t have a favorite, and for me, that’s always been Rubber Soul.

The Beatles had to bash out this album in a hurry, in October 1965, to rush some product into the shops in time for Christmas. They wrote seven of the songs in a week, pushing the deadline right down to the final hours. But they had a phenomenal hot streak. (Or should we say, it once had them?) Even the quickies have soul — like “Michelle,” a trifle Paul wrote in his teens for the specific purpose of wooing Liverpool art-student girls by pretending to be French.

But the thing that makes Rubber Soul stand out, head and moptops above the rest, is the singing, with these four boys mingling their voices, each sha-la-la and each na-na-na, each in-my-life and no-I-wouldn’t so charged with raw emotion. Their voices were changing from boys to men — Ringo and John were 25, Paul 23, George 22 — and you can hear their irresistible excitement that they can now emote as the world-weary men they always aspired to be. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

Just a year earlier, in tunes like “I’m a Loser” and “No Reply,” John was trying to sing like a gritty Dylan-esque folk rogue; now he not only had the voice to pull it off, he could write tunes to match. Paul had never sounded so rugged as he did in “I’m Looking Through You,” but never so boyish as he does in the middle eight of “Wait.” The way he purrs “I feel as though you ought to know,” he sounds so guileless, even though he’s cheerfully admitting he’s been cheating like crazy on the road. (That “I’ve been good, as good as I can be” is an all-time Paul line reading.)

George, after playing grown-up with his voice on Help! (with the magnificently boyish “I Need You” and “You Like Me Too Much”), got all the way there. Why was the Quiet One suddenly using words like “opaque” and “rectify”? Because his groovy mod wife Pattie Boyd bought him a thesaurus, hoping it would help him write some eloquent love songs to tell the world about her. It’s safe to say “Think for Yourself” wasn’t what she had in mind.

But that’s just the lead vocals, which are only part of the story here, because you can get lost forever immersing yourself in the background vocals. None of them are holding back, no matter whose song it is. Listen to what Paul adds to “Norwegian Wood” or “Nowhere Man” or “If I Needed Someone”; listen to what John brings to “You Won’t See Me” or “Wait.” In the vivid new remix from Giles Martin and Sam Okell, you can go deeper than ever into these harmonies. Related Content Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr to Reunite at Las Vegas Show in 2027 What's It Like to Write Songs With Madonna, McCartney, and the Stones? 50 Years Ago Today: Paul McCartney Wraps Up the Greatest Tour of His Post-Beatles Career Here Are the Best Podcasts About Songwriting

The lads were cranking around the clock to get Rubber Soul finished. They didn’t go into the studio with a plan to revolutionize pop music; they went in with a deadline. Nobody was asking for a great work of art— nobody except themselves, and their genius producer George Martin, who believed in them no matter what. The “harpsichord” solo in “In My Life”: That’s Mr. Martin, who went into the studio early, played his composed solo at half-speed on piano, sped it up to fit the tempo, then played it for the lads’ approval. That’s the spirit of collective make-it-work energy that made Rubber Soul come out as vibrant and fluent and unfettered as it is.

The pace was set right on the first day at Abbey Road, when John brought in two songs, from opposite sides of the genius spectrum: “Norwegian Wood,” a candidly introspective tale of getting outmaneuvered by a smarter operator, and “Run for Your Life,” a cheap Elvis joke that John somehow turned into one of his saddest, loneliest, most self-loathing vocals. “Run for Your Life” is the kind of song you’d bring to the studio if you scared yourself with how vulnerable you got in “Norwegian Wood.”

But both songs tell the truth about John’s miserable psyche in 1965. John was a recluse in his mansion, totally dependent on the Beatles as his only friends. He rarely even saw his wife or son without the TV blaring. He was a nowhere man, all right, and he told the truth about it in these songs. It might sound bizarre to think John brought in these different tunes the same day — yet it feels like “Run for Your Life” was a joke for him to hide behind, in case the other lads laughed at him for baring his soul in “Norwegian Wood.”

But they didn’t laugh. All four threw themselves into this song, wholeheartedly. George Harrison brought in an instrument he was still learning to play — he got it wrong, but came up with one of the most seductive sounds on any Beatles record, while Paul lifted John’s story with his ruggedly bruised vocals. (Rubber Soul is the place to start appreciating Paul’s underrated generosity as a team player; you don’t even notice him in “Norwegian Wood” or “If I Needed Someone,” until you do, but that’s when you realize how selflessly he’s elevating his fellow Beatles’ songs, and how bravely they wrote when they knew they could count on Paul covering their asses.)

There are no happy endings on the album — it’s the first Beatles album where none of the songs have “love” in the title, even though there’s a song about the word “love.” When Paul wrote his Rubber Soul songs, he was 23, the age Olivia Rodrigo is now — he really does seem pretty sad for a boy in love. (It’s the right age to be singing, “Love has a nasty habit of disappearing overnight.”)

But the dominant emotion here — in the voices and melodies far more than mere lyrics — is curiosity, as the boys chronicle a wide range of charismatic and complex women. Whether it’s John in “Girl” and “Norwegian Wood,” or George in “If I Needed Someone” and “Think for Yourself,” or Paul in “You Won’t See Me” and “I’m Looking Through You,” they’re on a quest to learn from these female characters, to communicate in their languages. (Even a goof like “Michelle” is about struggling to understand her native tongue; all we know about Michelle is she’s not learning Paul’s language at all.)

The first line of the album is John and Paul singing, “Asked a girl what she wanted to be.” In 1965, that was a question asked of boys, not girls. But the women on Rubber Soul have jobs, they have plans, they have interior lives and philosophical questions — none of them are waiting for a man, not even a Beatle.

On the final night of the sessions, they still needed two more songs to finish the album. So they showed up with two of their best: John’s “Girl” and Paul’s “You Won’t See Me.” You can hear the strain in their throats — you can also hear them revel in it. But all over Rubber Soul, you hear the Beatles listen to each other, openly imitating each other. They tell the truth about themselves by singing together.

As for “In My Life,” it’s the only Lennon-McCartney song where John and Paul seriously disputed who wrote it, which says a lot about how deep this song reached into both boys’ souls. John was eager to claim it for himself, while vacillating on how much Paul contributed. But in strictly musical terms, it has the Macca fingerprints all over it, especially the “all these places had their moments” bridge. The Beatles spend these tunes learning from each other, trying on each other’s personalities for size, wondering how it would feel to face the world with Paul’s jaunty confidence or John’s mean edge or George’s acerbic pout or Ringo’s good nature. “In My Life” is John openly envying Paul, imagining what it’s like to be as emotionally expressive and affectionate as his best friend, just like Paul spends “I’m Looking Through You” emulating John’s tough talk. Despite the title, “Girl” sure sounds like John singing about Paul — the boy who came to stay, the only one who could ever make John feel like a fool.

As always, whichever Beatles are singing, you can hear their drummer listen to them and support them. No group of singers ever had a drummer like Ringo, and everybody always does their bravest singing when they’ve got Ringo behind them. He works hard to make himself easy to overlook — he always makes it a point of professional pride not to call attention to himself. “Singers love the way I play,” he told me in 2018. “I don’t play all over them.”

But he’s the heartbeat of these tunes — the singers go to all the personal places they visit because they know Ringo is lifting them up. In a song like “In My Life,” he makes it easy for John to be vulnerable, guiding him through these really difficult memories. That’s why every cover version falls flat — the song doesn’t soar without him. You can make a case for Abbey Road or Revolver as his drumming-is-my-madness peak, but Rubber Soul really shines as Ringo’s greatest hit.

The Special Edition adds both sides of the stand-alone single they cut at the sessions, “Day Tripper” and “We Can Work It Out.” There’s an instrumental take of “Day Tripper,” for those of us who love the guitars and percussion but not the vocal. To my personal (and undoubtedly wrong) perspective, it’s one of the lamest Beatles vocals, one of the few where they come off as phonies. Paul trying to sound disdainful and unimpressed by a girl is just out of his vocal skill set, the equivalent of Mick Jagger trying to sound sincere and sensitive. There’s an acoustic take where John and Paul sound far more charming, treating it as a joke — John can’t stop laughing at the final verse, which deserved no better.

The U.S. record company, as usual, tried to water down the album with an American version. However, they failed, because this version was arguably even better, kicking off with the double-whammy of “I’ve Just Seen a Face” and “Norwegian Wood” — is there a more euphoric five-minute intro to any album? “I’ve Just Seen a Face” came out that summer, on the original U.K. Help! There’s a great scene in the early Rolling Stones documentary Charlie Is My Darling where Mick and Keith are on tour in 1965, bored and dour in their hotel room, until Keith begins strumming “I’ve Just Seen a Face” and they sing it together — suddenly, even these bitchy Glimmer Twins can’t help grinning. Trending Stories Noel Fielding Says He Regrets 'Horrible' Jokes He Made With Russell Brand After Old Clip Resurfaces Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters Files for Divorce From Fourth Wife Kamilah Chavis After 5 Years of Marriage Can Chris Van Hollen Really Unseat Chuck Schumer? Journey Go Their Separate Ways With Longtime Drummer

Capitol didn’t plan on making Rubber Soul sound like a “folk-rock” album — when they pulled “I’ve Just Seen a Face” and “It’s Only Love” from Help!, they had no idea how Rubber Soul would sound. Neither did the Beatles, who hadn’t written the songs yet. But it’s the only case where the butchered U.S. version might top the original. The American Rubber Soul turned out to be even more influential — it’s the one that inspired Brian Wilson to make Pet Sounds, the one that challenged Bob Dylan to make Blonde on Blonde, the one that blew the minds of Marvin Gaye and Carole King and Stevie Wonder and the Grateful Dead.

I’ve spent my entire life trying and failing to make up my mind which one I love better, so it’s good to have both of them bundled together on the Special Edition. But either way, it settles the question of the Beatles’ greatest album. In my life, I love Rubber Soul more.

#3290. Hackers Now Want Your Browser Sessions More Than Your Passwords, but You Can Stop Them

There’s a very organized dark web supply chain that attackers use to trade in stealer logs. Russian Market has effectively replaced Genesis Market as the new storefront for black hat cybercriminals, although much of the market has also shifted to private channels on Telegram.

According to threat analysts at DarkOwl, approximately 180,000 stealer logs were sold on Russian Market in just the first half of 2025. What's more, Russian Market is a well-designed storefront that users can access even without Onion links or the Tor browser. That means anyone could go there and buy a bunch of stealer logs to start attempting account takeovers at scale.

Meanwhile, Flare Research estimates that this isn’t even close to the actual scale of the threat, because 90% of stealer logs now surface privately on Telegram. There, automated chatbots let scammers shop for stealer logs like it’s Amazon, with options to filter by country, app, and account privilege. Logs sell for anywhere between $5 and $500 a piece, depending on the estimated value of the target accounts.

The easiest way to go about this is to take a look through all your active devices and their locations in your account settings on most websites. If you see a device or location you don’t recognize, you are likely the subject of an ongoing breach. However, keep in mind that this may not always be a reliable method if you use iCloud Private Relay or a VPN. Still, it's generally best practice to log out of all active sessions every once in a while and perform a fresh login to invalidate any unauthorized sessions.

Reset the passwords on your email account, enable two-factor authentication for added protection, and sign out of all sessions before doing a fresh login. Your email inbox is the single point of entry for most attacks because that’s where most websites send their verification codes or magic links.

Sign out of all active sessions on every account that you suspect is compromised. This will log out any attackers who are currently on a hijacked browsing session.

Change your passwords on every platform in order of priority. Start with banking websites, cloud storage providers, and password managers first.

Look through each compromised account’s third-party integrations and app permissions. Revoke access if you can’t recognize an app, or it looks suspicious. Also make sure to rotate any API keys that you’re currently using, since those may have been compromised as well.

But while the initiative has already been open-sourced, no other major online provider has begun offering native support for it as of this article. That means DBSC’s security benefits are limited to Google services like Gmail and Docs, Chrome for Windows, and third-party websites that offer single sign-on (SSO) options for your Google account. We might see a wider rollout in the near future, though.

#3287. Looze Cannon Was Rapping Before You Met ‘Big Michael’

The latest viral earworm on social media has an uncanny resemblance to the King of Pop. “Big Michael Michael,” first born as a freestyle on the musician and content creator Looze Cannon’s livestream, has taken the internet by storm. Delivered in a cotton-soft register not unlike Jackson’s, the track has gone on to top the iTunes Hip-Hop/Rap chart and inspire a lip-sync video from Lil Baby. Earlier this month, Looze Cannon brought his “Big Michael” character to G Herbo’s show at Chicago’s United Center, performing in front of a nearly sold-out crowd.

“G Herbo, I think he did a post where he was singing a song, and the next thing I know, my management was just telling me, ‘Hey, Herbo wants you to come out at the United Center in Chicago and perform,’” Cannon tells Rolling Stone. “I was like, ‘What?’ I thought everybody was playing, but it was real. We got in the Sprinter and we drove straight from Detroit to Chicago. And next thing I know, I was on stage, man, having the biggest moment of my life.”

The crowd size was the biggest Looze Cannon, who’s been rapping in Detroit since the 2010s, had ever performed in front of. “I’ve been around some big crowds because I’ve always been on stages and stuff like that, but that was the biggest thus far, was the G Herbo show,” he says. “That was the most I’ve ever performed in front of all at once.”

Cannon is among a new generation of artists who, in addition to releasing music, have developed a career livestreaming and making online video content. In his videos, he uses an AI face filter to perform as Jackson and various other characters on his livestreams. After first premiering the character early last month, he officially released the single “Big Michael Michael” on October 24.

“I had no clue that ‘Big Michael Michael’ would take off like that because it was just me playing around,” he says. “And so I just look back and I just say, wow, man, I can’t blame anybody but God, man, because I’ve been doing this for a long time and to see how this transition to what it is, it’s unexplainable.”  Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

A Detroit native, Cannon’s been releasing music since at least 2016, when he put out Looze Minded. In 2020, he released Lil Glen, followed by Now or Never in 2023. Even so, he says detractors try to discredit his current moment as merely a viral gimmick. “I knew my wittiness and my funniness would help push the music because what I learned throughout the years is you got to get the people,” he says. “A lot of rappers, sometimes they focus on being too cool and trying to put off an image that they think will propel them into stardom or whatever, and people lose sight of being who they are.”

While he says he isn’t a Michael Jackson impersonator, he credits the singer with making him want to pursue music.

“I’m a big Michael Jackson fan. Michael was the reason why I even really wanted to do music,” he says. “I knew that there’s so many different versions of the impersonators out there and things like that, but I analyzed the game. What is it that no one is doing? And I just hit the live button, man, with that filter on and just blacked out. I just blacked out and it happened.”

He’d already been trying out other characters on livestream. “I have over 10 characters and I haven’t really unleashed all of them yet,” he says. “I was on an app called BIGO LIVE where I did multiple characters.”

Cannon’s other characters include a version of Dr. Seuss who tells stories in costume. He says he’s preparing to shoot a movie based on another of his characters. For TikTok, he went with Jackson. “I chose Mike on the TikTok side because I just knew the shock value of what it would do,” he says. Related Content Paris Jackson Calls Estate Executor’s $109 Million Fee Request ‘Offensive,’ Seeks Reduction Michael Jackson’s Legendary Super Bowl Halftime Show Is Getting Its Own Documentary Noel Gallagher’s ‘MTV Unplugged’ Acoustic Guitar Fetches $300,000 at Auction Jaafar Jackson Hopes 'Michael' Sequel Will Give 'More Insight' Into Allegations From Singer's 'Point of View'

“I thought back on just implementing my music into what I do, or pretty much taking the characters that I do and implementing what I really do into those characters,” he says. “And so that’s where the freestyling and doing the song, the parody songs, came into play.”

Cannon says commenters have mocked his advice to “be yourself” because he’s impersonating someone else. “They’re only looking at the surface of the filter,” he notes.

“None of them do what I do,” Cannon says of people who think his content doesn’t require skill or talent. “And it’s a reason for that because I’m actually being Looze Cannon. And I think that’s what the game is missing is just originality.”

“I always tell people, ‘Put a Prince filter on and see if you can dance with me in the same type of ring,’” he adds. “And if you can’t do that, then what you’re saying is just, in my eyes, just hate.”

When I suggest that the filters are still new, Cannon corrects me. “It’s not really new,” he says. “Anybody can put a filter on, but how can you bring it to life? People get so lost on, ‘Oh, I can put a filter on,’ and things like that. But after you put the filter on, you only have the attention span of a person for at least five to 10, 15 seconds max to lock them in, or they swiping somewhere else.”

“It takes a certain type of charisma to bring the filter to life because people want to really get into what’s happening,” he continues. “But if you’re just banking on a filter and talking like your regular self or not performing in a certain way, then it means nothing.”

Cannon is independent and says he’d been selling downloads directly to fans before “Big Michael Michael” took off.

“I’ve been pretty much direct-to-consumer because I’m an independent artist and I always was in the streaming world,” he says.

The appeal was how much a small group of fans could bring in. “I had to get the mindset of, you know what? Hey, if I have 50 loyal fans that’ll buy my download for $1.99, I’m beating a majority of the people that’s getting 100,000 streams,” he says. “But in the midst of that, I understand the times that we’re in and you got to play ball sometimes. And how this record took off, I knew that I had to service the platforms. So I did it, but I’ve always been direct-to-consumer for a long time now.”

He says the new listeners are finding his older music, too. “I’m actually seeing the numbers of my other songs and they are picking up. They skyrocketing right as well,” he says. “So people hear ‘Big Michael Michael’ and they’re like, ‘Oh wait, he has more music. Let me go check it out.’”

“My Spotify is up, my Apple Music is up,” Cannon adds. “I’m seeing people actually post my other records and doing videos to my other songs, so that’s a good sign.”

He says Snoop Dogg, Timbaland, and Usher have reached out, along with comedians Tiffany Haddish and Funny Marco. “I got a lot of celebrity friends now,” he says. “Uncle Snoop Dogg, that’s my guy.” Trending Stories Noel Fielding Says He Regrets 'Horrible' Jokes He Made With Russell Brand After Old Clip Resurfaces Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters Files for Divorce From Fourth Wife Kamilah Chavis After 5 Years of Marriage Can Chris Van Hollen Really Unseat Chuck Schumer? Journey Go Their Separate Ways With Longtime Drummer

“I’ve been in the studio working with a few different talented artists from the Eric Bellingers, the Roscoe Dash, and many more,” he adds. “I’ll just say more for right now.”

Now, Looze Cannon is planning a project to follow the single. “Yes, I’m definitely about to drop a project because it’s time,” he says. “It’s time to show everybody that outside of my content that I do on social media, I’m a serious artist and I’m going to show the world that now that I got the eyes, it’s time to show them the prize.”

The entire Hisense U8 lineup is currently discounted ahead of Black Friday, with prices starting at $797.96 for the 55-inch model (down from $1,424.99) and going up to $2,798.99 for the massive 100-inch version (originally $3,999.99). Regardless of which size you choose, Amazon throws in free delivery to the room of your choice, a service that normally costs $19.99.

Brightness is the U8QG’s main advantage, with the manufacturer estimating up to 5,000 nits of peak brightness, while PCMag measured around 3,200 nits when reviewing the 65-inch model. Actual performance will vary with the picture mode and content, but either figure points to strong highlights in Dolby Vision and HDR10 video. Its Mini-LED local dimming also produces deep blacks, although some light bloom can appear around bright objects on dark backgrounds. Audio-wise, its built-in 4.1.2-channel system, which includes surround channels, a subwoofer, and upward-firing speakers, gives movies more scale than typical TV speakers, though a separate sound system can still offer clearer separation and a broader soundstage.

The U8QG also has plenty to offer gamers using a current-generation console or a capable gaming PC. It supports refresh rates up to 165Hz, variable refresh rate, and AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, with a measured 4.3 milliseconds of input lag at 1080p and 120Hz and 10.1 milliseconds at 4K and 60Hz. Those results should make controls feel responsive, even during fast-paced games. There’s also a side-mounted USB-C port that accepts DisplayPort video, while Google TV handles streaming alongside Apple AirPlay and Google Cast. The biggest inconvenience is the limited selection of three HDMI ports, since a console, soundbar, and streaming device would occupy all of them.

#3284. watchOS 27.3: Three new features coming soon to Apple Watch

watchOS 27.3 will launch to all users next month and introduce these three new Apple Watch features.

Siri AI keeps getting new features and also expanding to more languages. And in watchOS 27.3, the assistant will improve in both categories.

watchOS 27.3 upgrades Siri AI with new app actions across built-in apps like Calendar, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, and Weather. With these capabilities, Siri on your wrist can do more than ever.

There are also four new Siri AI languages supported in watchOS 27.3: Chinese (traditional), Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

For the latest Apple Watch models, watchOS 27.3 adds a new Audio Intelligence feature called Live Rewind. Per Apple’s website:

Live Rewind recalls what was just said in the last 15 seconds by showing a text snippet on your Apple Watch when you double-press the Digital Crown, so you can catch something you missed or are less familiar with. You can ask Siri about the content of the snippet or simply save it to the Siri app.

I’m curious to see how useful this proves in everyday life. When Apple demoed the feature in September, it showed Live Rewind being used at a restaurant when an Apple Watch user missed part of the server’s menu explanation. Asking the server to repeat what they said seems like an easier solution, but perhaps there are other occasions Live Rewind will come in handy.

It won’t be for everyone, but I’ve been testing watchOS 27.3’s new Siri Recap feature and really love it.

Siri Recap only works on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and it’s off by default. But if you have one of those models and enable the feature, Siri can create automatic logs of what’s happening in your day-to-day life.

Most of the time, you won’t need to reference any of the recaps and they’ll be automatically deleted after a week. But based on my experience with the feature, Siri Recap definitely comes in handy at times when trying to remember key details from conversations.

Which of watchOS 27.3’s new features are you most interested in? Let us know in the comments.

#3278. Apple offers a military discount, here’s how to get it

If you’re a member of the U.S. military, Apple offers an easy way to save 10% on eligible products and accessories. It’s available to current and veteran members of the U.S. military and their immediate family members living in the same household. While you’ll need to verify your eligibility to access the discount, the process is simple. There are also a few limitations you’ll want to know about before placing an order. Here’s everything you need to know.

A 10% discount is available to current and Veteran members of the US Military, National Guard and Reserve. Immediate family members who reside in the same household are also eligible.

Verification is handled through ID.me. Creating an ID.me account is free, and current military members can verify their service using their .mil email address. Veterans can enter details of their service information for ID.me to verify, or upload images of official documents (such as a DD-214) for ID.me to review and confirm their eligibility. Once you’re verified, your ID.me account can also be used to access military discounts from other retailers and services that support ID.me verification.

Once verified, you can start shopping by visiting Apple’s Store for Veterans and Military. The discount only applies to Apple products and accessories (including Beats) so third-party products aren’t eligible. Apple services, such as Apple Music and iCloud+, are also excluded. Orders can be shipped directly to you, or you can choose in-store pickup if the product is available at a nearby Apple Store.

This is probably the biggest catch. Apple specifically says ACMI isn’t available when shopping through the Veterans and Military Store. You can still earn 3% back in Daily Cash with Apple Card, but you lose the option to finance your purchase at 0% interest over several months. Apple Upgrade also isn’t available when purchasing through the military store.

The only way to get the military discount is to make your purchase through Apple’s website in a browser. The Apple Store app isn’t an option, which means you also can’t take advantage of Apple’s “Get Ready” feature to select your iPhone model, color, storage capacity, and carrier ahead of pre-orders opening. Instead, you’ll have to navigate Apple’s website on launch day, when demand is high and server traffic can make checkout more challenging. Whether the 10% savings is worth giving up the convenience of a potentially quicker checkout is ultimately up to you.

The military discount can’t be combined with carrier promotions or discounts on iPhone purchases. You can still trade in your existing iPhone through Apple and receive the applicable trade-in value, but you can’t take advantage of carrier-specific trade-in offers, like promotions that give you a larger credit when you trade in an eligible device and activate or upgrade a line.

These purchase limits reset on January 1 each year.

Apple’s military discount is a useful perk, especially if you’re buying a product at launch and want to save 10% right away. However, it’s worth comparing prices with other retailers before you buy, since sales and promotions can sometimes beat Apple’s discount. The military store also comes with a few limitations, so you’ll want to weigh the savings against the features and payment options you’re giving up. Even with those caveats, 10% off can make a real difference on an expensive Apple purchase.
